rule: Sovereign Cloud Advisory placement ladder (PLAN S7, D17, D19). Rungs are cumulative: a kind of data needs every control of its minimum rung and of the rungs below it. The minimum rung is the one whose level equals the data's required level. A 'platformMove' rung cannot be reached in a provider's standard regions when the provider's parent is outside the data's allowed zone: the data moves to an offering at that rung (LTM judgement, owner approval at Gate S7; counsel confirms R4 at S10). The ladder changes the advice, never the maturity score (D3). Only generally available options meet a rung; announced, preview and per-engagement options are shown, labelled (D24). R3 needs day-to-day operations and support in the zone through a local entity; supervised access is R2 (D25). No offering is presented as meeting R4: the matrix lists facts for counsel (D26). Government clouds are R3 for US data, with an eligibility caveat (D27). Options are examples of service families, each sourced in the claims register with a review date; they are listed in a fixed order that does not rank providers.

rungs.label: Standard region
rungs.means: Any standard region; no sovereignty controls required

rungs.label: In-zone region with guardrails
rungs.means: A standard region inside the allowed zone, with policies that block deployments elsewhere; backups and replicas in the zone too

rungs.label: Customer-held keys and approved access
rungs.means: R1, plus keys held outside the provider, provider access only with your approval, and the provider's data boundary where one exists

rungs.label: Sovereign offering run in the zone
rungs.means: R2, plus a service operated and supported only by staff in the zone, employed by a local entity under local law

rungs.label: No foreign control in the provider chain, or disconnected
rungs.means: R3, plus no company in the provider chain is owned or controlled from outside the zone, or the system is disconnected
